1.explanation:
1. gather/gather-runner-test.js – validates how the gather phase collects artifacts (e.g. traces, devtools logs) across frames. We need to see whether subframes are even surfaced here.
2. network-records-to-devtools-log.js – converts raw networkRecords into a DevTools log format. If iframe requests are dropped or mis‐attributed, metrics will be skewed.
3. computed/page-dependency-graph-test.js – builds the dependency graph of all network requests and resources. Ensuring subframe nodes/resources appear here is crucial to include their cost.
4. computed/resource-summary-test.js – summarizes all resource sizes and timings. If iframe resources aren’t included, weight and timing won’t factor into metrics.
5. audits/metrics-test.js – exercises the core performance metric calculations (FCP, TTI, Speed Index, etc.). It shows what inputs are expected and if they currently assume only the main frame.
6. runner-test.js – covers the end‐to‐end run (gather → audit → report). This is where aggregation across frames (and potential multi‐url runs) should be hooked in to reflect iframe impact.
1.bug_scenario:
The example shows a parent page (index.html) that embeds a slow‐loading, artificially throttled iframe (huge-dom.html). When Lighthouse runs on the parent, its Performance score (~71) ignores the iframe’s heavy/slow resources. Running Lighthouse directly on the iframe yields a much lower Performance score (~39). In other words, subframe load impact isn’t bubbled up to the parent’s metrics, producing misleadingly good scores.

Key on‐screen elements:
- A top‐level iframe HTML element in index.html
- Parent page metrics panel (showing 71)
- Child (iframe‐only) metrics panel (showing 39)
- Metrics like First Contentful Paint, Speed Index, Time to Interactive, etc., that should aggregate across frames but currently do not
